This mean that the financial obligation of rural electric cooperative which are private are to be borne by the PSALM Corporation, a public corporation. rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING A ONE (1)-YEAR REGISTRATION OF INCUMBENT TEACHERS WITHOUT EXAMINATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Board for Professional Teachers, under the general supervision and administrative control of the Professional Regulation Commission is hereby authorized to register incumbent teachers without examination for another year, commencing after the issuance of the necessary rules and guidelines for the effective implementation of this Act: Provided, That the incumbent teachers are qualified to be registered without examination in accordance with the provisions of Section 26 of Republic Act No. 7836, otherwise known as the "Philippine Teachers Professionaliza tion Act of 1994": Provided, further, That there shall be no other registration of incumbent teachers without examination upon the expiration of the one-year period provided under this AAct.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05411

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION TWENTY OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Section 20 (a) and (e) of R.A. 7160 exempts from reclassificatio n or conversion of such "agricultural lands distributed to agrarian reform beneficiaries pursuant to R.A. 6657 otherwise known as The Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law." However, the word "distributed" as used in this section is not defined. Since lands acquired by the government through CARP coverage are distributed and resold to the agrarian beneficiaries, it is implied that unless the original landowners had been duly compensated for their property, the government can not legally distribute said lands to the agrarian beneficiaries without violating the constitutional right of the landowners to due process under the Philippine Constitution. Hence, the need to ameend this Section in order to make the exception more specific, thereby avoiding injustice.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2002-01-22

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A FISHERIES AND MARINE SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL IN EVERY LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE COUNTRY, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Fishing is an occupation wherein most Filipinos are engaged in a primary means of livelihood. The immediate mobilization of manpower in the fisheries field will surely accelerate economic growth in the country. Hence, the need to upgradethe secondary curriculum to integrate thereto science and technology subjects that will provide students with skills and training in fisheries and marine sciences, and broadened the students' knowledge, capabilities and appreciation for fishereies and marine technologies.

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO BE KNOWN AS `THE MARITIME LIENS AND SHIP MORTGAGE ACT OF 2002
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Mortgage Law has not helped ship owners to gain access to more affordable financing because foreign banks, generally, do not accept a mortgage over a vessel constituted under Philippine law. There, apparently, is a problem in the concurrence and preference of credits as provided in the law. There are presently no laws governing this sector of the industry as this has always been viewed as part of ship owning and ship operation. > Thus, this proposed measure.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2002-01-22

rows.abstract: "Domestic Shipping Development Act of 2002". This bill seeks to substantiate the policy of the State to: (1) Promote Filipino ownership of vessels operated under the Philippine flag; (2) Attract private capital investment in the shipping industry; (3) Effect the upgrading of existing domestic merchant marine ______ to international standards; and (4) Ensure the continued viability of domestic ship operators.

This proposed measure seeks to grant the following incentives to shipbuilding and ship repair yards: (1) Exemption from import duties and taxes; and (2) Exemption from the Value-Added Tax. Penalties for violation of this Act are likewise provided.

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE EXTENSION OF EXEMPTION FROM INCOME TAX ON INCOME DERIVED FROM PHILIPPINE OVERSEAS SHIPPING, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7471, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PHILIPPINE OVERSEAS SHIPPING DEVELOPMENT ACT
rows.abstract: Rationale: An Overseas Shipping Act was passed in 1955 granting incentives to the sector. Terms for acquiring vessels under this Act were a disincentive to the acquisition and disposition of vessels because it lacked the flexibility needed by ship owners to quickly purchase and dispose of vessels. The incentives under this law expired in 1985. New incentives were given to the sector in 1992. The incentives granted by this law will expire in 2002. > We need strengthen our overseas shipping so that vessels owners will be encouraged to serve more of our trade and carry at least 50% of our import and export trade by 2010.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2002-01-22

rows.abstract: "Dual Citizenship Act of 2002". This bill seeks to remedy the apparent unjust treatment suffered by our expatriates and overseas workers and their families who are considered second class citizens in their own homeland by extending them dual citizenship and enabling them to enjoy full civil and political rights such as the right of suffrage/or to voted for public office under certain conditions. > It is the policy of the State that natural-born Filipino citizens are not automatically deprived of their Philippines citizenship by their acquisition of another foreign citizenship. rows.abstract: Rationale: It has been almost ten (10) years since the formal establishment of the Sangguniang Kabataan. rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 316 OF ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES INCREASING THE PENALTY THEREFOR(RE: PENALIZING AN ACT OF PRETENDING TO BE AN OWNER OF REAL PROPERTY AND CRIMES RELATED THERETO)
rows.abstract: Rationale: The act of pretending to be an owner of real property and conveying, selling encumbering or mortgaging the same as well as encumbering a real property knowing that the same is already encumbered is penalized under Article 316 of the Revised Penal Code (Act 3815). The said law however, hardly has any teeth as it failed to deter further violations of the same. This is because conviction under the said law is merely punished by an imprisonment of arresto mayor in its minimum and mediumperiod or from one (1) month to four (4) months only. Those charged in court for the said violation is not even required to post bail for his/temporary liberty.> This bill seeks to restrain further violations of the above stated lay by increasing thee penalty in the crime called other forms of swindling.

rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING DUAL CITIZENSHIP TO NATURAL-BORN FILIPINOS WHO ACQUIRED FOREIGN CITIZENSHIP AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Dual Citizenship Act of 2002". The bill seeks the enactment of a dual citizenship law, essentially granting natural-born Filipinos the privilege to retain or regain Filipino citizenship after having acquired or obtained citizenship of another country.> Natural-born citizens of the Philippines who became naturalized citizens of a foreign country are deemed to have retained or re-acquired their Philippine citizenship without renouncing their foreign citizenship upon the effectivity of this Act.Philippine citizenship shall not be deemed lost by virtue of naturalization in a foreign country or by operation of law of another country unless the person categorically and unequivocally renounces under oath his Philippine citizenship before a Phillippine consular official abroad or any public officer authorized to administer an oath except when such renunciation was an oath of allegiance required by the foreign country for naturalization purposes.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04720

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE PHILIPPINE OVERSEAS EMPLOYMENT AGENCY (POEA) TO INCLUDE IN ITS PROGRAM FOR OVERSEAS EMPLOYMENT THE MANDATORY TEACHING OF BASIC SELF-DEFENSE TECHNIQUES FOR WOMEN APPLICANTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: For the past decades now, there had been alarming upsurge of violence especially against women, our overseas women employees abroad included. Because of thier apparent vulnerable conditions in the workplace, they have often become prone to assault, harassment, rape, and other forms of violence. These alleged forms of violence against our women overseas employees can be averted by a program that will require our women overseas employees to face not only the psychological and emotionalchallenges confronting them while productively employed abroad apart from their respective families.
